findings.title: Public send exceeds the three-second API contract
findings.observation: The representative public send_message operation completed successfully in 3116 ms, while the approved public semantic API contract requires at most 3000 ms.
findings.trigger: Start with WeChat frontmost in Contacts and execute public send_message for a visible conversation.
findings.impact: Consumers cannot rely on the documented three-second upper bound for the complete convenience API.

evidence.description: One authorized public command returned success true and submitted true with top-level duration 3116 ms.
The same command measured 1042 ms for chats AXPress, 482 ms for the current-frame click, 517 ms for clipboard draft, and 319 ms for Return submission.
evidence.reference: private live service output; no raw payload committed

evidence.description: The reviewed design requires each public WeChat semantic API to complete within three seconds in the representative smoke environment.

findings.remediation: Remove bounded transport or startup overhead, with a warm Accessibility action transport as the first candidate, without bypassing app identity, target identity, current-frame coordinate, or title postcondition checks.
findings.verification: Add deterministic worker success, timeout, and subprocess fallback tests; run package suites and preflight; then obtain new authorization and prove public send_message completes within 3000 ms.

required_actions.action: Implement a safety-equivalent bounded performance optimization and prove the public send path completes within 3000 ms.

WeChat in Contacts with a visible target is representative of the approved smoke environment.
